paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

model_annotations.German: The plot titled “Errors (RTE)” illustrates how an error metric for the RTE task varies with adapter rank. The x-axis is labeled “Rank” and shows four discrete values (4, 16, 64, 256) displayed at equal spacing consistent with a logarithmic progression (multiplying by 4 each step). The y-axis has an unlabeled numeric scale with visible tick labels at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9 on a linear scale, spanning approximately from about 0.25 up to about 1.0. A single series is drawn as a thick solid black line connecting large green circular markers, with black vertical error bars at each point (with small horizontal caps). The marker at rank 4 is near 0.35 (error bar roughly from about 0.29 to about 0.41), the marker at rank 16 is slightly lower near 0.33 (error bar roughly from about 0.28 to about 0.38), the marker at rank 64 rises to around 0.41–0.42 (error bar roughly from about 0.34 to about 0.49), and the marker at rank 256 increases further to around 0.63–0.64 (error bar roughly from about 0.59 to about 0.66), producing a slight dip from 4 to 16 followed by increases through 64 and 256.
